st: Put the potatoes, [[5 cups]] water and [[1.5 tsp]] salt in a heavy pot. Boil 20 minutes until very soft.
Lift out the potatoes with a slotted spoon, keep the water in the pot, and mash the potatoes well.
Return the mash to the water and bring back to a simmer.
Add [[1.5 cups]] cornmeal in a thin stream without stirring, then make a hole in the middle and let it steam, covered, for 10 minutes on low heat.
Beat hard with a wooden spoon for 5 minutes until smooth, thick and creamy.
Stir in [[4 tbsp]] butter and [[1 cup]] crumbled cheese until melted in.
Serve hot topped with [[0.5 cup]] kajmak or cream.

ing: cleaned, bodies in rings, tentacles halved
or fish stock plus 1 tbsp lemon juice
st: Heat the stock in a pot and keep it barely simmering.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes, then the garlic 1 minute.
Add the squid and cook 5 minutes until opaque. Remove half and set aside.
Add [[1.5 cups]] rice and stir 2 minutes until glossy. Pour in the wine and cook until absorbed.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] squid ink. Add hot stock one ladle at a time, stirring, waiting until each is nearly absorbed.
Continue for 20 minutes until the rice is creamy and just tender, using about [[5 cups]] stock.
Return the reserved squid. Season with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and stir in [[2 tbsp]] olive oil.
Rest 2 minutes, sprinkle with [[0.25 cup]] parsley, and serve.

ing: finely grated, plus 1 diced for serving
st: In a bowl, combine the beef, lamb, garlic, grated onion, [[0.5 tsp]] baking soda, [[2 tsp]] salt, [[1 tsp]] pepper and [[1 tsp]] paprika.
Add [[0.25 cup]] sparkling water and knead by hand 5 minutes until very sticky and well mixed.
Cover and chill at least 1 hour.
Wet your hands and shape the mix into small fingers about 3 inches long and 1 inch thick.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high.
Cook 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and the center reaches 160°F (71°C).
Warm the flatbreads on the grill for 1 minute each.
Serve the ćevapi in the bread with diced onion and [[0.5 cup]] kajmak or sour cream.
Rinse jarred grape leaves in hot water and drain. Trim stems.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil and cook the onions 6 minutes until soft. Stir in [[1 tbsp]] paprika and take off the heat.
Mix the onions with the beef, rice, parsley, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Place a leaf shiny side down. Put a spoonful of filling at the stem end, fold the sides, and roll up firmly. Repeat.
Line a pot with spare leaves and pack the rolls tightly seam side down.
Pour in [[2 cups]] hot water and [[2 tbsp]] lemon juice and weigh the rolls down with a plate.
Cover and simmer gently 1 hour 15 minutes until the rice is cooked and the beef reaches 160°F (71°C).
Serve warm with yogurt if you like.
Rinse the mussels and discard any with open or cracked shells that do not close when tapped.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the garlic 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in [[1 cup]] crushed tomatoes and [[2 tbsp]] bread crumbs. Cook 3 minutes.
Pour in [[1 cup]] white wine and bring to a boil. Add [[0.25 cup]] parsley.
Add the mussels, cover, and cook on high for 5 to 6 minutes, shaking the pot, until the shells open.
Discard any mussels that stay closed. Season with [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and salt if needed.
Sprinkle with [[0.25 cup]] parsley and serve with the sauce and bread.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour, [[2 tsp]] yeast, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt in a bowl.
Add [[0.5 cup]] warm milk, [[0.5 cup]] yogurt and the egg. Stir to a soft, sticky dough.
Knead 5 minutes, cover, and let rise 40 minutes until doubled.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil to 350°F (175°C) in a deep pot.
Pull off walnut-size pieces of dough and stretch them flat.
Fry in batches for 2 minutes per side until puffed and deep golden. Drain on paper towels.
Serve warm with [[0.5 cup]] honey and [[1 cup]] crumbled cheese.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pan and cook the onions 6 minutes until soft.
Add the beef and cook 8 minutes until browned and cooked through to 160°F (71°C). Season with [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] pepper. Cool.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Oil a large baking pan.
Brush 2 sheets of phyllo with oil. Spread a line of filling along one long edge and roll into a thin tube.
Coil the tube into the pan. Repeat with the rest of the phyllo and filling, packing the coils together.
Whisk [[1 cup]] warm water with [[0.5 cup]] yogurt and pour it over the burek, then brush with [[4 tbsp]] oil.
Bake 40 minutes until deep golden.
Rest 10 minutes and serve warm in squares.
